reports.summary: Bloody May, student sit-ins and the squatter movement: Berlin has long been a hotbed for working-class organizing and radical left-wing politics.

reports.title: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania: SPD seeks to fend off AfD
reports.summary: For nearly three decades, the Social Democrats have governed Germany's northeastern state. If they can fend off the AfD, the result may boost the fortunes of the German government's junior coalition partner.

reports.title: Ever more Israelis moving to and investing in Cyprus
reports.summary: Over the past three years, more and more Israelis have been purchasing property and investing in Cyprus, with many moving to the island permanently. How has this changed the Cypriot economy and how are locals responding?

reports.title: Women's football in Germany booming, but still much to do
reports.summary: Women's football is growing rapidly, particularly in Germany. Nevertheless, equal pay and investment remain major talking points.

reports.title: Strait of Hormuz attacks spill oil into Persian Gulf
reports.summary: As war disrupts one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, satellite images reveal that oil is spreading toward protected coral reefs and mangrove forests.

reports.title: Airport malaria in Germany remains infrequent
reports.summary: An outbreak of malaria at Frankfurt Airport this summer has raised alarm. Experts believe parasites probably arrived in a passenger's luggage. But with the onset of fall, the risks of contracting the disease are low.

reports.title: Fact Check: False video alleges Berlin votes destroyed
reports.summary: A video claiming to show AfD postal ballots being destroyed has gone viral ahead of Berlin's September 20 election. DW Fact Check examines the footage, the accounts sharing it and how widely it is really being viewed.

reports.title: German police probe arson attack on Wuppertal synagogue
reports.summary: The man detained shortly after allegedly trying to set fire to Wuppertal's synagogue made antisemitic comments to the arresting officers, prosecutors say. The 37-year-old Afghan citizen also had knives in his apartment.

reports.title: Canada and EU: A look at the bloc's special relationships
reports.summary: Though Canada may be some distance from Europe geographically, closer political ties are in the cards. With talk of an associate membership, DW takes a look at other arrangements the EU has with particular countries.

reports.title: Dual citizenship means Germany now in competition for talent
reports.summary: Coach Jürgen Klopp has named several players to his first Germany squad who are eligible to play for other countries. Some still aren't committed to playing for thje national team long-term.

reports.title: Beethoven and Andy Warhol: Rebel icons on show in Bonn
reports.summary: The new exhibition "Beethoven by Warhol" at the Beethoven House in Bonn presents the pop artist's late masterpiece: a picture of Ludwig van Beethoven. The exhibition shares the story of the work with the public.

reports.title: 'No compromises': Far-right AfD has few potential partners
reports.summary: Germany's far-right AfD party is riding high after its latest electoral triumph in Saxony-Anhalt. But one question remains: Does it actually want to govern?

reports.title: UN Crime Congress: Technology is transforming crime – and the response to it
reports.summary: Sitting in her Vienna office ahead of a pivotal UN gathering in Abu Dhabi, Monica Juma is focused on a simple reality: crime has evolved faster than many of the institutions designed to combat it.

reports.title: ‘Violence will only defer a problem’: UN Assembly President on trust, AI and lessons from the Rohingya crisis
reports.summary: Khalilur Rahman took the gavel as President of the UN General Assembly's 81st session amid what he calls a crisis of confidence in the organization he has served – in one capacity or another – for 35 years.

reports.title: Security Council LIVE: UN peacekeeping under pressure
reports.summary: UN peacekeepers have increasingly been sent into places where there is no peace to keep – under resourced, outgunned and exposed to violence they are not equipped to counter. The Security Council meets this afternoon in New York to confront that problem, with Secretary-General António Guterres briefing ambassadors on how to close the gap.

reports.title: Sexual violence against civilians and POWs in Ukraine widespread and ‘abhorrent’
reports.summary: Over 1,000 cases of sexual violence against civilians and prisoners of war (POWs) in Ukraine have been documented from the start of Russia’s invasion to the end of July this year.

reports.title: Less than 4 years from development goals deadline, progress shows what’s possible
reports.summary: For Benin, making progress on the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) has meant finding new ways to finance development.

reports.title: Women and girls pay high price in DR Congo Ebola outbreak
reports.summary: The deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has taken a disproportionate toll on women and girls, many of whom are on the frontlines caring for patients as well as their own families despite the high risk of infection.

reports.title: Haiti: Child malnutrition crisis worsens amid escalating violence
reports.summary: Haiti is facing a worsening child malnutrition crisis, with an estimated 253,725 children aged 6 to 59 months projected to suffer from acute malnutrition between June 2026 and May 2027, new UN-backed analysis has revealed.

reports.title: Nepal floods: ‘Apocalyptic’ destruction signals wider climate threat across Himalayas
reports.summary: The catastrophic flooding that swept away entire villages in northern Nepal could occur again in the country or elsewhere in the Himalayas due to climate change.

reports.title: Yemen’s humanitarian crisis growing by the hour amid spike in displacement
reports.summary: People displaced by the renewed fighting in Yemen have described fleeing for their lives amid shelling and gunfire, aid agencies reported on Friday, while highlighting the dramatic increase in humanitarian needs in the country and in Djibouti, where thousands have sought shelter.

reports.title: VAR's mission creep a problem for football
reports.summary: After a decade of use, questions around VAR in football are louder than ever. Has the technology strayed too far from its remit?

reports.title: Organized crime and drug-related deaths rise Germany
reports.summary: In the annual report on organized crime, German police say cocaine is a danger for the state and society and cases of money laundering have increased.

reports.title: Russian birth tourism to Brazil increases
reports.summary: Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and stricter regulations in Argentina, more and more Russians are choosing to travel to Brazil to give birth to children, who will obtain Brazilian nationality.

reports.title: A war-fatigued and anxious Russia picks a new parliament
reports.summary: Fuel shortages, drone strikes and mobilization rumors are fueling anxiety and war fatigue in Russia. As support for peace talks grows among Russians, the Kremlin is watching closely ahead of parliamentary elections.

reports.title: Alexander Ovechkin backs Putin party in campaign video
reports.summary: Ice hockey legend Alexander Ovechkin has lent Vladimir Putin's party a helping hand in its parliamentary election campaign. That's in keeping with a pattern of support by an athlete who claims not to be political.

reports.title: Judges: As AfD ascends, Germany must bolster justice system
reports.summary: German judges and prosecutors warn that the coalition needs to reform the laws covering state prosecutors to prevent "extremists in government" from abusing the legal system.

reports.title: As global crises grow, Germany cuts development aid
reports.summary: The budget of Germany's Economic Cooperation and Development Ministry is set to shrink for the fifth consecutive year. Aid organizations warn that the cuts will have severe consequences for millions of people.

reports.title: New UN system platform puts millions of data points at users’ fingertips, says Guterres
reports.summary: How do you make sense of a world facing interconnected crises, from poverty and hunger to climate change, if the facts are scattered across dozens of different places?

reports.title: World News in Brief: Winter aid for Gaza, West Bank; Haiti food production; migrant deaths at sea; human rights funding
reports.summary: The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) is seeking to raise $97.5 million to protect 540,000 children and their families in Gaza and the West Bank from harsh winter conditions in the coming months.

reports.title: Gender equality woefully off track, new UN report reveals
reports.summary: At the current rate of progress, gender equality would take 171 years to achieve, a new UN report finds as institutions built to advance gains are being defunded and demobilised.

reports.title: UN fact-finding mission on Iran focuses on plight of civilians
reports.summary: The Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran confirmed that civilians in the country suffered serious human rights violations and “crimes against humanity committed by their government,” while finding "reasonable grounds" to believe that the United States committed “war crimes” in the context of its ongoing conflict with the Islamic Republic.

reports.title: Guterres calls for action as hate speech spreads across new platforms online
reports.summary: The UN Secretary-General has called for concerted action by governments, technology companies and civil society to stamp out hate speech, emphasizing that “its toxic message is spreading fast and striking deep”.

reports.title: Security Council LIVE: Syria’s transition in the spotlight
reports.summary: While Syria is making progress in its political transition, the Security Council is meeting to hear briefings and discuss the situation on the ground, including recent reports of deadly armed clashes with an ISIS-affiliate terrorist group in the south and protests over rising fuel prices.

reports.title: Yemen escalation displaces more than 57,000 children: UNICEF
reports.summary: Renewed fighting in Yemen is deepening an already severe humanitarian crisis in a country where more than 12 million children depend on aid, after more than a decade of conflict.

reports.title: As freshwater reserves shrink, countries must prepare for a new water reality
reports.summary: The world is entering a period in which abnormal water supplies are becoming the norm, with river flows, groundwater and glaciers all showing signs of sustained disruption, the UN weather agency warned on Thursday.

reports.title: Klopp wants Germany's football team to 'reclaim the flag'
reports.summary: Jürgen Klopp, Germany's new head coach, says he wants his team to reclaim pride in being German after recent political developments.

reports.title: Serbian President Vucic criticizes Kosovo war crimes verdict
reports.summary: The conviction of four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has drawn sharply different reactions across the Balkans. Serbia has accused the court of failing to fully address crimes against Serbs.

reports.title: King Charles, Earl Spencer clash over Diana death once again

reports.title: Jews once lived lived here: When houses tell stories
reports.summary: Time and again, residents tracing the history of their homes discover the lives of Jewish predecessors who fled or were deported amid stories of suffering and loss.

reports.title: Jürgen Klopp's first Germany squad includes 44 players
reports.summary: Germany's new head coach Jürgen Klopp has named a huge squad for his first four games, splitting them into two groups. A host of new faces is included.

reports.title: Saint, sinner or feminist icon: How Mary Magdalene's image evolved through time
reports.summary: From "Apostle of the Apostles" to prostitute, Mary Magdalene has been assigned a wide variety of roles, as a new exhibition shows.

reports.title: How climate change worsened Nepal's deadly mountain collapse

reports.summary: Residents of Piddington, a tiny, remote village in Oxfordshire in England, have staged a "referendum" on leaving the UK. They are objecting to plans to open an asylum reception center at a disused military base nearby.

reports.title: Can Canada and the EU deepen ties to counter Trump?

reports.title: Chancellor Merz seeks CDU support amid far-right AfD surge
reports.summary: Following the CDU's crushing defeat in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, many are expressing doubts about the party's leader, Chancellor Friedrich Merz. But the CDU doesn't appear to have a viable alternative.

reports.title: Shock in Kosovo as Hague convicts former President Thaci
reports.summary: The conviction in The Hague of former President Hashim Thaci and three former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has caused consternation in Kosovo — both among political leaders and on the streets. DW reports from Pristina.

reports.title: British-American writer Bonnie Greer dies aged 77

reports.title: After Neuer: Who will be Germany's new No. 1 goalkeeper?
reports.summary: Following Manuel Neuer's retirement, there are many candidates to succeed him, but which goalkeeper will Jürgen Klopp choose? What factors will play a role? And will Neuer's future have an indirect influence?

reports.title: Poland reaffirms support for Ukraine after drone strikes
reports.summary: After Russia's recent drone attacks on targets close to the Ukraine-Poland border, Warsaw has doubled down on its support for Kyiv and pledged a "nonprovocative but serious response" to Moscow.

reports.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing rapidly, raising questions about how societies and governments can capture its benefits while managing risks that often extend beyond national borders.

reports.title: Repression continues in Venezuela in the face of ‘appalling’ human rights violations

reports.title: AI, climate and conflicts top Guterres’s agenda ahead of General Assembly
reports.summary: Ahead of the UN General Assembly’s high-level week, Secretary-General António Guterres said the world had entered “an era of deep uncertainty” and urged governments to embrace international cooperation to address global threats.

reports.title: Global Gender Gap Report: Women's hard-won gains 'fragile'

reports.summary: Heat waves, wildfires and floods have cascading economic impacts, causing incomes to decline and the price of basic goods to rise. The trend will escalate as temperatures continue to increase.

reports.title: Turkey's rights groups, EU call out LGBTQ+ crackdown

reports.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz wants to provide relief to motorists. But exactly how this is to happen remains unclear.

reports.summary: A recent crackdown on the LGBTQ+ community in Turkey is symptomatic of a wider rights regression, according to experts. It's worse under authoritarian regimes, but why is it such a popular policy for these states?

reports.title: Why the era of cheap government debt is over
reports.summary: US debt has topped $40 trillion. How risky is the country's growing debt burden. And will investors keep funding Washington's deficits?

reports.title: Socialist Left Party holds slim lead in polarized Berlin polls
reports.summary: The results of the Berlin election are as hard to predict as ever. Three parties are vying for first place, including the socialist Left Party and the far-right AfD. But one issue is most important to Berliners.

reports.title: Germany news: Merz to cancel UN trip amid party infighting
reports.summary: Germany's chancellor nixxed his trip over doubts about his leadership after party losses to the AfD in state elections. Meanwhile, Defense Minister Pistorius is in Washington for talks with his US counterpart.

reports.title: Can popular state premier Schwesig hold off the far-right AfD?
reports.summary: Manuela Schwesig has led Germany’s northeastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania since 2017. Will the center-left premier be able to stop the far-right AfD from emerging as the strongest force in Sunday’s election?

reports.summary: A major outage has hit parts of the Dutch railway system after objects were found placed across lines, authorities say. The company responsible for rail infrastructure says it suspects deliberate wrongdoing.

reports.title: Europe launches two climate observation satellites
reports.summary: The European Space Agency has put two satellites into orbit to take a closer look at the impact of climate change. One of them will focus particularly on plant life.

reports.title: EU seeks Arctic strategy amid growing power rivalry
reports.summary: Russia's aggression, Trump's threats against Greenland and the race for critical raw materials are pushing the Arctic to the top of Europe's agenda.

reports.title: Ukraine, Russia set for new round of US-mediated talks

reports.title: Women's Basketball World Cup: Can Germany harness a boom?
reports.summary: Germany thrilled fans at the Women's Basketball World Cup. But even if this sparked a boom in the women's game, the infrastructure simply isn't ready for it.

reports.title: The Crusades: How a medieval holy war still shapes politics

reports.title: Germany's Zverev wins US Open in golden year

reports.title: The 'end of an era' as Goethe-Institut in Russia closes
reports.summary: The Goethe-Institut was one of the last German institutions still operating in Russia. However, following Moscow's decision to close its offices, all employees will have to stop working by September 13.

reports.title: How Celine Dion became a pop culture icon across generations
reports.summary: As the global star kicks off her anticipated Paris residency, here's how Celine Dion managed to gain younger followers while keeping her loyal older fans.

reports.title: How Belarusians still find hope in a silenced country
reports.summary: The documentary "Letters from the Silenced Country" depicts the ongoing repression under the authoritarian regime. Director Andrei Kutsila talked to DW ahead of the film's Venice premiere.

reports.title: Why we're still looking for dark matter

reports.title: LIV Golf in financial turmoil: What's next for the sport?
reports.summary: Six months after Saudi Arabia pulled funding from the breakaway organization, LIV Golf have filed for bankruptcy protection. Several of the world's best players signed on to LIV, so where does that leave golf?

reports.title: Conspiracy theories can provide answers but not peace

reports.summary: Traffickers are making big bucks smuggling millions of critically endangered eels across continents, using suitcases on planes and legal loopholes to deliver them to dinnerplates. Where are the smuggling hotspots?

reports.title: The Bayeux Tapestry in London: What's behind the hype?
reports.summary: The exhibition of the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum is eagerly anticipated across the UK, as the medieval masterpiece is considered by many to be a symbol of the country's identity.

reports.title: EU sports commissioner says FIFA is 'damaging to football'
reports.summary: Speaking to DW, EU Commissioner Glenn Micallef hit out at world football's governing body over its "poor governance."

reports.title: Afghanistan's women: A national soccer team without a home
reports.summary: The Afghan women's national football team has finally been officially recognized by FIFA. Now the players want to make history both on and off the field.

reports.title: PISA 2025 results: Reading and math scores plummet worldwide
reports.summary: The PISA 2025 results reveal record-low student performance, with digital distractions and AI use raising concerns. Germany is faring worse than ever.

reports.title: Elversberg: Bundesliga newcomers from tiny town make waves
reports.summary: A team from a small southwestern German town of just 7,000 inhabitants made history by sealing promotion to become the 59th club to play in the Bundesliga. Elversberg has got off to a memorable start.

reports.title: Egg freezing in women's football: Choice or pressure?
reports.summary: Spain's football federation is set to join a handful of clubs in paying for female players to freeze their eggs. Experts have welfare concerns.

reports.title: Werner Herzog: Germany's wild man of cinema is back
reports.summary: As his latest movie, "Bucking Fastard," premiered at the Venice Film Festival, DW talked to the boundary-breaking director.

reports.title: Croatia: Toxic waste protest draws tens of thousands
reports.summary: The Zagreb demonstrators demanded that the government come up with a plan to clear illegal toxic waste in 20 days. Prime Minister Plenkovic has promised to tackle the issue.

reports.title: Germany: From emigration to immigration destination
reports.summary: Migration is a sensitive topic in Germany, with public debate dominated by the fear of uncontrolled immigration. But over two centuries, millions of Germans emigrated in search of a better life.

reports.title: The hidden environmental cost of AI data centers
reports.summary: As data centers multiply to meet AI demand, they're straining power grids, draining water supplies and reshaping the land and air around them.

reports.title: Germany: Is Saxony-Anhalt's economy really struggling?

reports.title: Why North Korea's women's football team is so good

reports.title: 2026 Beethoven Festival evokes a sense of home
reports.summary: The motto of this year's classical music festival in Bonn is "Home/At Home," featuring musicians from diverse cultures presenting pieces from their homelands.

reports.title: How Volkswagen's huge workforce became a costly burden
reports.summary: The struggling German carmaker plans to cut up to 100,000 jobs from its 630,000-strong workforce. How did VW's headcount get so bloated, and will the cuts be enough to survive the Chinese EV onslaught?

reports.title: Is Germany's economic slump finally over?
reports.summary: Despite a slew of negative headlines, the German economy has posted its best figures in years. There are reasons for optimism, but structural issues remain.

reports.title: Austria women ice hockey team fight for future generations
reports.summary: Austria are getting ready for their first Women's Ice Hockey World Championship. But preparations have been overshadowed by a dispute about conditions, pay and getting men's cast-off kit. A solution now looks in sight.

reports.title: Women's football: Anyomi, London City and the German exodus

reports.title: Can communities be protected from melting glaciers?
reports.summary: Rising temperatures are increasing the risk of floods and avalanches in mountain regions. The disaster in Nepal and Tibet shows the urgent need for solutions, and the tools that could help save lives.

reports.title: Can new Apple CEO John Ternus fix the tech giant's AI woes?
reports.summary: John Ternus is just the third Apple CEO in 30 years. His primary challenge is to correct the company's faltering AI strategy to preserve its position as a big tech leader.

reports.title: At Venice Film Festival, politics take center stage
reports.summary: With works about Gaza, Ukraine and Elon Musk, political cinema is in the spotlight at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

reports.title: Canada's Carney holds firm against Trump tariffs
reports.summary: Canada is facing new US import penalties after Prime Minister Mark Carney refused to match US tariffs on China. Other countries are watching as the Trump trade clash turns into a fight over economic sovereignty.

reports.title: Inside the sea cucumber smuggling boom

reports.title: Ailing Djokovic 'despised' every moment of US Open defeat
reports.summary: Novak Djokovic has exited in the first round of a Grand Slam for the first time in over two decades. Could time — or an unknown health condition — be catching up with the Serbian tennis legend?

reports.title: EU wants drones to spray pesticides, but it could backfire
reports.summary: The EU wants to lift a decades-old ban on spraying pesticides from the air, allowing drones to be used for greater precision. But experts warn the plan could lead to even more pesticides being used in agriculture.

reports.title: This extremely successful author polarizes German readers
reports.summary: She's young and she says what she thinks: Caroline Wahl is topping Germany's bestseller lists with her novels. But she has also faced a public backlash.

reports.title: What 'The Odyssey' can teach us about climate chaos
reports.summary: The Bronze Age collapse may have started with a water crisis. The droughts of today raise the unsettling question of whether it could happen again.

reports.title: Influential humanists: These are the winners of the Goethe Medal 2026
reports.summary: The prestigious German cultural award recognizes the artistic work and commitment to cultural dialogue of Arvo Pärt, Anita Raja and Prodromos Tsinikoris.

reports.title: Germany's military wants to recruit tech-savvy gamers
reports.summary: The Bundeswehr has been a fixture at Gamescom, Cologne's video game trade fair, for years. But critics say military recruitment does not belong at an entertainment convention.

reports.title: Spain: Thieves steal Bronze Age gold in lightning raid on Villena Museum

reports.title: Tragedy in Nepal: How do flash floods happen?
reports.summary: When flash floods sweep through the Himalayas, there is often little time to react. Scientists are working to understand the risks and improve early warning systems.

reports.title: Andre Rankel named Germany's new men's ice hockey coach
reports.summary: Germany's men's ice hockey team has appointed a new head coach following a string of dissappointing tournaments. He's two decades younger than the man he's replacing but he has no previous experience as a head coach.

reports.title: New study shows German football remains male-dominated
reports.summary: The top leagues of German football remain a largely male environment. A new study reveals that only seven clubs have women in upper management levels.

reports.title: Venus' US Open invitation raises questions about wild cards
reports.summary: Although her current world ranking wouldn't allow it, Venus Williams is set to play singles in the US Open – thanks to a wild card. Who gets these coveted spots—and how?

reports.title: The great lake divide: Collapse vs. comeback
reports.summary: As some of the world's biggest lakes vanish in real time, others are proving that recovery is still within reach.

reports.title: Why social media addiction is so hard to regulate

reports.title: Was the heat of this summer really 'normal?'
reports.summary: Some political messaging denies the role of human-caused climate change in this summer's extreme heat. The science tells a different story.

reports.title: Gamescom 2026: What's next for the gaming industry?

reports.title: Why Germany's Volkswagen could cut 100,000 jobs
reports.summary: Europe's biggest automaker, Volkswagen, faces Chinese competition, high costs and US tariffs. What could its restructuring mean for the German car industry?

reports.title: Can new US sanctions cripple Iran's shadow economy?
reports.summary: The US is expanding sanctions on Iran's financial networks, targeting crypto, gold, aviation and shipping. DW spoke with analysts about what could change.

reports.title: Trees are vital for cooler cities, but they need help too
reports.summary: Record-breaking heat and drought are putting urban trees at risk. Experts explain how to protect these essential assets and build city forests that can withstand the climate challenges ahead.

reports.title: Scientists discover new 'immune hubs' in skull bone marrow
reports.summary: "Immune hubs" that actively defend the brain have been discovered in mouse skull marrow. Similar cells exist in human skulls, but their role remains unclear.

reports.title: Spiraling health costs force Iranians to delay care
